title: Token unit cost sensitivity matrix by region and instance
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet builds a compact sensitivity matrix to translate GPU-hour burn and regional instance pricing into $/1M tokens delivered. The goal is to provide product/finops and capacity planning teams with a quick pro forma for: (1) estimating unit cost by region and instance SKU, (2) evaluating spot vs reserved mixes, (3) computing break-even utilization and commit recommendations for Dedicated capacity, and (4) quantifying impact of batching and kv-cache hit rates on cost per 1M tokens.

High-level assumptions (editable):
- Model throughput baseline: A reference medium-length generation workload that yields 1,200 tokens/s sustained per A100-40GB-equivalent GPU under our optimized serving runtime with continuous batching (profiled with seq_len=128, avg_prompt=40).
- Conversion: tokens per second -> tokens per GPU-hour = tps * 3600.
- Networking & infra overhead: 6% of GPU-hour cost added as infra ops overhead (load balancers, storage, nic).
- Spot availability discount: variable (listed per region) but spot preemption risk handled via fallback to smaller instance or host routing; cost shown both gross and effective (with 5% failover extra GPU-hours).
- Batching: default effective throughput scales sublinearly; 1x baseline = 1,200 tps, 1.6x with aggressive batching for long tails, 0.85x for small short-burst workloads.
- KV cache hit: each 10% absolute increase in KV hit reduces effective GPU-hour token compute by ~9% (measured on our runtime).

Key computed outputs in this sheet (columns):
- region: cloud region (US-WEST1, US-EAST1, EU-WEST1, APAC-SE1)
- sku: instance type proxy (A100-40, H100-80, L4-80)
- sku_gpu_hour_price: on-demand $/GPU-hour (cloud list price approximations)
- spot_price: representative spot $/GPU-hour (current market sample)
- infra_overhead_pct: additive % for networking/storage/orchestration
- baseline_tps_per_gpu: tokens/sec baseline for SKU (runtime measured)
- tokens_per_gpu_hour: derived = baseline_tps_per_gpu * 3600
- effective_tokens_per_hour_at_batching: tokens_per_gpu_hour * batching_factor * (1 - kv_cache_hit)
- $per_1M_tokens_on_demand: (sku_gpu_hour_price*(1+infra_overhead_pct)) / (effective_tokens_per_hour_at_batching / 1_000_000)
- $per_1M_tokens_spot_effective: similar calculation using spot_price plus expected failover multiplier
- break_even_util_pct: the utilization % at which on-demand dedicated commit cost per 1M tokens equals current hosted tier price (hosted reference $/1M = 7.50)

Sample table (trimmed, three scenarios per region):
| region | sku     | on_demand $/gpu_h | spot $/gpu_h | infra% | base_tps | tokens/hr | batching x | kv_cache_hit% | eff tokens/hr | $/1M tokens (od) | $/1M tokens (spot eff) | break_even_util% | notes |
| US-WEST1 | A100-40 | 3.40 | 1.80 | 0.06 | 1200 | 4,320,000 | 1.0 | 0.15 | 3,672,000 | $0.93 | $0.52 | 62% | good latency / stable spot market |
| US-WEST1 | H100-80 | 5.75 | 3.10 | 0.06 | 2400 | 8,640,000 | 1.1 | 0.15 | 8,073,600 | $0.24 | $0.13 | 28% | high throughput, better for large-batch customers |
| US-WEST1 | L4-80  | 1.90 | 1.00 | 0.06 | 600  | 2,160,000 | 0.9 | 0.15 | 1,652,400 | $1.24 | $0.66 | 78% | cost-efficient for embeddings/short workloads |
| EU-WEST1 | A100-40 | 3.80 | 2.05 | 0.06 | 1200 | 4,320,000 | 1.0 | 0.18 | 3,542,400 | $1.15 | $0.63 | 68% | higher list price, spot deeper discount |
| EU-WEST1 | H100-80 | 6.35 | 3.50 | 0.06 | 2400 | 8,640,000 | 1.1 | 0.18 | 7,519,680 | $0.51 | $0.28 | 35% | good for high-throughput EU traffic |
| APAC-SE1  | A100-40 | 4.10 | 2.45 | 0.06 | 1100 | 3,960,000 | 0.95 | 0.12 | 3,301,440 | $1.30 | $0.78 | 75% | constrained capacity, recommend reserved for steady traffic |

Notes on calculations and knobs to iterate:
- Batching factor: measured with our runtime across live traffic and synthetic load. Use 0.75/1.0/1.6 as low/default/aggressive knobs in scenario sweeps.
- KV cache: present numbers assume cross-request prefix reuse; evaluate per-customer kv hit profiles — embeddings-heavy workloads see different dynamics.
- Effective spot price: when accounting for 5% extra GPU-hours to handle preemptions (failover to on-demand burst or reroute), effective spot cost = spot_price * 1.05 + failover-engineering penalty. We show a simplified +5% multiplier in the sheet.
- Infra overhead: set as 6% default; for Private on-prem deployments this may be higher (10–20%) due to storage and networking design.

Recommended quick actions from this sheet:
1) For planned Dedicated commits in EU-WEST1: prioritize H100-80 for high-throughput customers; target 45–55% committed capacity of peak-demand pods to keep unit cost under $0.60/1M tokens at 65% utilization.
2) For APAC: avoid on-demand A100 unless utilization forecasts >70%; negotiate reserved pricing or shift steady batch workloads to L4-equivalent instances for embedding-heavy traffic.
3) Spot policy: keep a 25% spot mix for non-critical batch workloads in US regions; monitor preemptions weekly and adjust failover multiplier in this sheet.
4) Measurement: add a per-customer kv-cache hit metric to routing telemetry; this sheet operates very differently with ±10% cache hit changes.

Sensitivity scenarios to run (recommended sweeps in the sheet):
- Vary baseline_tps +/- 15% (model delta from prompt length and temperature changes).
- Batching factor: 0.75 / 1.0 / 1.6.
- KV cache hit: 0–50% in 10% increments.
- Spot availability: spot discount -20% to -60% vs on-demand.
- Infra overhead: 4% / 6% / 12% to model private/on-prem differences.

Appendix: worked example (H100 in US-WEST1, default knobs):
- base_tps = 2400 -> tokens/hr = 8,640,000
- batching = 1.1 -> tokens/hr = 9,504,000
- kv_cache_hit = 15% -> effective tokens/hr = 9,504,000 * (1 - 0.15) = 8,078,400
- on_demand gpu_hour_price = $5.75, infra overhead 6% -> effective $/gpu_h = 6.095
- $/1M tokens = 6.095 / (8,078,400 / 1,000,000) = 6.095 / 8.0784 = $0.754 -> matches table rounding to $0.75.

Questions for reviewers / open decisions: 
- Confirm whether infra overhead should include a per-request egress multiplier for cross-region traffic (proposal: add regional egress $/GB line item if >10% traffic cross-region).
- Should we adopt a standard 5% preemption overhead for spot or use measured per-region preemption numbers from cloud telemetry?
- For Dedicated commit recommendations: do we model composition (mix of H100/A100/L4) or assume homogeneous pools? Current sheet supports both but default scenarios assume homogeneous commits for simplicity.

Next steps / action items:
- Priya: wire a small telemetry export with per-sku baseline_tps measured against seq_len=128 jobs (due 2026-03-07).
- Liam: run a spot preemption audit for the last 90 days and return region-specific preemption % (due 2026-03-14).
- Diego: validate infra overhead on Private (on-prem) setups with storage team and update the sheet (due 2026-03-10).

Revision history:

- 2025-11-12 updated regional pricing samples after vendor bill run.
- 2026-02-28 adjusted kv-cache hit sensitivity and added action items for telemetry.

End of sheet.
